hook_text: Ever wonder why prices suddenly shoot up when everyone gets paid?
clip_script: [Tutor face to camera, energetic] Ever wonder why meat prices shoot up when everyone gets paid? [Cut to whiteboard showing axes] Here is the secret. It’s all about shifts in demand! [Animate D1 and S1 intersecting at E1] This is our initial market equilibrium for beef. [Point to E1] Price is set. Now, consumers get a bump in income. Because beef is a normal good, people can afford more of it. [Animate D1 shifting to the right to D2, turning blue to highlight] This is not a movement along the curve, the ENTIRE demand curve shifts right. But notice, the supply curve hasn't moved! It still costs the same to produce beef. [Animate E2 appearing higher up the supply curve] So, what happens? Our new demand hits the old supply at a higher point. The result? Higher equilibrium price and a higher equilibrium quantity traded. [Fast zoom back to Tutor] That’s the power of a demand shift. Know the difference between a shift and a movement, and you master the market.
visual_style: Fast-paced whiteboard animation with clear, high-contrast labels (D1 to D2 in bright blue) and quick zooms to the tutor's face.
pacing: Rapid and highly visual, perfectly timed to the 60 second mark
